fixes.explanation: Jesus says, “Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.” No bulbs, no batteries, no feeling around the wall for a switch. Just following Him. I spent years in the dark at the back of a junk drawer, and that promise lands.

Close neighborhood, friend, but a different house. In this verse the promise is about darkness and the light of life, and troubles aren't mentioned. Jesus does talk about troubled hearts at another time: “Do not let your hearts be troubled.” (John 14:1). Stick with the light here.
The Sabbath doesn't come up in this passage. The Pharisees, strict religious leaders, say He is testifying about Himself, and that His testimony is not valid. That's the complaint the text gives.

Jesus doesn't agree with them. He says the opposite: “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going.” They called it not valid, and He says it is valid. That's a hard no, straight up.

They ask, “Where is Your Father?” and Jesus answers, “You do not know Me or My Father…” Then He adds, “If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.” So the question gets an answer, and the answer is about knowing Him.
That's true, friend. The Pharisees ask where His Father is. Jesus answers, “You do not know Me or My Father. If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.” Both parts happened just like that.

The text says it plainly: “…no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.” He's teaching in the open, near the treasury, and still no one seizes Him. The text gives one reason, and it's His hour.
No feast rule is mentioned in this verse. The passage says no one seized Him because His hour had not yet come. That's the reason the text gives, so that's the one we keep.
Abraham, Israel's forefather (Genesis 12:2), doesn't come up in these verses. What Jesus says they must believe is “…that I am He…” The question on the table is who Jesus is.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), isn't named in this passage. Jesus does mention “…your own Law…” earlier (John 8:17), but the belief He asks for here is different: “…unless you believe that I am He…” It all comes back to Him.

They ask, “Who are You?” and Jesus replies, “Just what I have been telling you from the beginning…” So He points back to what He's been telling them from the beginning. That's not a brand new announcement, friend.

The text tells us, “They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.” Jesus is speaking about the One who sent Him, and it sails right past them. Sometimes the answer is sitting right in front of you. I've done that with my own mustache.
This one is true as written. The text says, “They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.” He is talking about the One who sent Him, and they don't catch it.
Jesus says, “…I always do what pleases Him.” Always, not once in a while. He says the Father has not left Him alone because of it. The reason is right there in the verse, friend.
The text says, “As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.” After all that back and forth, many believe. That's a good thing to hear, and I love hearing it.
The text doesn't say they walked away. It says, “As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.” Believing is what the text says.
No one asks for a sign in this verse. The text says that as Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him. What happens here is belief.
